lawyer:
M Moniruzzaman Khan with Morshed Ahmed Khan, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner. 
Md Khalequzzaman, Advocate ----- For the objector.
parties:
Tahmid Ahmed ------ Petitioner
vs
Jalaluddin Jaffar Ali Hussain ------ Objector
full_judgment:
Tahmid Ahmed, a shareholder-director of tile Company filed the aforesaid application for holding the Annual General Meetings of the Company for the years from 1982-1997 after condoning the delay in holding such meetings. It was contended in that application that the Company carried on its business smoothly until 18-5-1983. But could not hold its Annual General Meetings for the years 1982-1997 due to misconstruction of a status quo order obtained by a shareholder Jalal Uddin Jaffar Ali Hussein in Title Suit No.188 of 1983. Jalal Uddin Jaffar Ali Hussein filed the said suit challenging the resolution dated 8-5-1983 passed by the Company in an Extraordinary General Meeting whereby he and his father were removed from their office as directors of the Company. The above title suit was decreed on 17-8-1997 setting aside the said resolution whereupon the Company had filed an appeal, which is now pending in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka. 

 3. Jalal Uddin Jaffar Ali Hussein as objector opposed the holding of the annual general meetings for the aforesaid years by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that the majority shareholders of the company led by Tahmid Ahmed illegally removed him and his late father Jaffar Ali Hossain by the aforesaid resolution dated 8-5-1983 with a view to exclude them from the management of the affairs of the Company. He and his father filed the above suit and obtained an order of status quo so that they could continue to take part in the management of the affairs of the Company. In spite of such order of status quo Jalal Uddin Jaffar Ali Hussein and his father were not allowed to take part in the management of the Company for the last 14 years. Tahmid Ahmed and others being apprehensive of the fact that Jalal Uddin Jafor Ali Hussein and his late father would be re-instated as directors consequent upon the suit being decreed hurried to this Court for obtaining necessary order for holding annual general meetings for the years 1982-1997 by condoning the delay in order to cover up their past misdeeds for the last 14 years. 

 11. Mr Moniruzzaman Khan, learned Counsel for the petitioner in reply submits that the statements contained in the order dated 19-3-1998 of this Court that the company shall allow the objector to participate in the affairs of the company in his position as a director and/or share-holder and in the annual general meetings in accordance with law" cannot be considered as a direction and as such holding of the said meetings in non-compliance of the same would not be in violation of the order dated 19-3-1998. Mr Khan next argues that even assuming without conceding that the said statement was a direction of the Court, but in view of the expression "and/or "used in the statement the Company had an option to consider the Objector Jalaluddin Jaffar Ali Hussein as a share-holder and not a director particularly when the decree obtained in the suit was under challenge in the appeal now pending. Hence, the non-service of notice of the board meeting on the objector will have no effect to render the proceedings of the aforesaid board meeting held on 2-3-1998 nullity and consequently the annual general meeting held on 29-9-1998 should be taken to have been duly called, held and conducted as per direction of this Court. 

 15. It is admitted that the, objector Mr. Jaialudddin Jaffar Ali Hossain and his late father was removed from the position of directors of the Company by a resolution dated 8-5-1983. Consequent upon which the said objector and his father filed Title Suit No. 188 of 1983 challenging the said resolution and obtained an order of status quo. This suit was finally decreed in their favour vide judgment and decree dated 31-7-1997 and the Company filed an appeal against the said judgment and decree which is still pending. It is also admitted that there has been no order of stay of the-operation of the said judgment and decree in the said appeal. In this background of the matter and also in view of the contentions of the objector that he and his father were excluded from the affairs of the Company for the last 15116 years since the date of their removal from the office of the directorship, this Court by order dated 19-3-1998 while directing to call annual general meetings of the Company by condoning the delay gave ancillary direction to allow the objector to participate in the affairs of the Company as a director and in the annual general meetings as a share-holder, because such ancillary or consequential direction was required to be made to ensure neutrality. 

 16. Propriety arid the necessity of passing such ancillary or consequential direction is not too far to seek in the facts and circumstance of the case. It is clear from the respective cases put forth by the parties that there are two groups of share-holders in the Company and the directors representing major share-holding interest are allegedly trying to run the affairs of the Company to promote and secure their group interest in utter disregard and at the cost of the minority share-holding interest represented by the objector. The group of share-holders represented by the Objector and his late father comprises of only 17% of the total share-holding interest in the company the other group by virtue of their majority in the share-holding interest of the company succeeded in excluding the objector and his father from the affairs of the company for about long 14/15 years. The objector representing the minority group of share-holders succeeded In obtaining the decree in the aforesaid suit, In this view of the matter, this Court while directing to call the annual general meetings also gave ancillary and consequential directions to allow the objector to participate in the board meeting as a director prior to holding the annual general meetings of the company.
